about: Every question GridSchool may ask a student, in chunks. The AI picks the next chunk and may reword a question for the person, but never changes what it measures, and may add at most 2 follow-ups per chunk. Logic: data/intake/intake.mjs. Server checks: server/intake.py. Plan: the GridSchool Complete build plan doc.

chunks.title: Where you stand
chunks.unlocks: Your draft map and top bottlenecks
chunks.intro: Just six quick questions. Your map draws itself as you answer.

chunks.title: Goals and limits
chunks.intro: Tell us what a good next job looks like for you, and what it can't cost you.

chunks.title: Where it stops
chunks.intro: Let's look at where your applications go and what comes back.
chunks.done: Your search channels are on your map.

chunks.title: Your proof
chunks.intro: Let's look at the work you've shipped that someone else could open and check.
chunks.done: Your proof is on the map.

chunks.title: Your presence
chunks.intro: This is what a recruiter sees in their first seven seconds. We'll handle the rewriting and the design.
chunks.done: We're preparing your profile now. It shows up on your map when it's ready.

chunks.title: Your interviews
chunks.intro: Tell us about the interviews you've had and where they ended.
chunks.done: Your interview prep is on the map.

chunks.title: Your targets
chunks.intro: Tell us where you'd like to work, and where you wouldn't.

chunks.title: What you're into
chunks.unlocks: Project ideas, posts and drafts that sound like you
chunks.intro: What you like working on, the look you like, and how you write. Project ideas, posts and drafts start from here.
chunks.done: Your interests and voice are on your map.

questions.prompt: Which is closest to you right now?
What role do you want next?
What level are you aiming for?
How long have you been looking?
About how many applications have you sent in that time?
When you apply, how far do you usually get?

options.label: I get a recruiter call, then nothing
I make it to the technical round
I reach the final round, then get a no
I get offers, just not the right ones

questions.prompt: What base salary are you aiming for, and what's the least you'd accept?
questions.help: In US dollars per year. A rough number is fine.

questions.prompt: Which ways of working are open to you?
Which city do you live in or near?
Do you need visa sponsorship to work in the US?

options.label: Not now, but I will later

questions.prompt: How soon do you need income?

options.label: I can wait for the right role

questions.prompt: Would contract or short-term work help in the meantime?
How many hours a week can you give the search?
Where have you been sending applications?
About how many of those got a reply from an actual person?
Do you tailor your resume for each role?

options.label: For the ones I really want
I use one resume for everything

questions.prompt: How recently were the jobs you apply to usually posted?
Has a company ever told you why they passed on you?
questions.help: If so, paste what they said as closely as you can.

questions.prompt: Name up to three things you've built that real people used.
questions.help: One line each. Work projects, side projects and school projects all count.

questions.prompt: Do you have any numbers that show their impact, like users, speed, money or time saved?
questions.help: Only include numbers you could stand behind in an interview.

questions.prompt: Share any links where someone can see your work, like GitHub, a live demo or a write-up.
How do you use AI tools when you code?

options.label: Daily, and I check what they write
I build AI features or agents

questions.prompt: Have you been responsible for keeping software running in production?
questions.help: For example, being on call, fixing it when it broke, or monitoring it.

questions.prompt: What's the link to your LinkedIn profile?
Add screenshots of your LinkedIn profile, or your LinkedIn data export.
questions.help: The top section, About and Experience are enough. We read them for you, so you don't have to retype anything.

questions.prompt: Add your current profile photo, if you have one.
Add your current LinkedIn banner, if you have one.
Want us to make a professional headshot from your own photos?
questions.help: It will still look like you, with the same face, age and features. You'll see it before anyone else does, and you decide whether to use it.

questions.prompt: Add 1 to 3 clear photos of your face.
questions.help: Face a window, hold your phone at eye level, and take off any sunglasses. We only use these to make your headshot.

questions.prompt: How often do recruiters message you?
Tell us about your last few interviews: the company, and the round where it ended.
Which parts of interviews are hardest for you?
How have you practiced so far?
In one or two lines, how do you answer "tell me about yourself"?
Are there companies you'd love to work at?
Are there any companies or industries you won't work for?
What size of company suits you?
Are there any industries you know well or care about?
questions.help: For example health, finance, logistics or games: whatever you've worked close to.

questions.prompt: What technical things do you most enjoy working on?
questions.help: A few, separated by commas. For example agents, data pipelines, developer tools or game engines.

questions.prompt: What are you into outside of work?
questions.help: A few, separated by commas. Hobbies, sports, causes, anything you'd happily talk about.

questions.prompt: Which 3 to 5 words describe the look and feel you like?
questions.help: For example calm, bold, playful, minimal or technical. We use them for your banner and portfolio.

questions.prompt: Whose style do you like? Name sites, designs or people.
questions.help: Links or names both work, one per line.

questions.prompt: Paste something you wrote: a post, an email or a message.
questions.help: A few sentences or more, in your normal voice. Drafts we write for you will sound like this.
